Open Settings and select the root folder of R5Reloaded and/or R5Flowstate. ReMap detects platform and RPAK folders automatically.

Choose an Asset Cache folder on a drive with about 10 GB of free space, then save it. This folder stores indexes, extracted models, textures, and thumbnails. Changing it does not move or delete the previous cache.

Save the game paths. The first-time setup button can then prepare the selected installation safely.

Use File > New map, choose the target game and the Apex map you want to edit. The target stays attached to the project.

Open the Indexing page, enable the map archives required by the project, then apply the changes. Common assets are included automatically. The first indexing pass may take a while; ReMap remains usable while thumbnails continue in the background.

Search the model library, then double-click a card or drag it into the scene. Use W, E, and R for move, rotate, and scale. F frames the selection.

Use the hierarchy to rename, group, reorder, disable, or reparent objects. Ctrl+D places a duplicate and Escape cancels placement. Save regularly with Ctrl+S. Personal assemblies let you reuse a complete selection later.

Open the generated game code from the toolbar or File menu. Review the Scripts and ENT tabs, then use Build and install map.

Native ENT optimization is enabled by default. Unsupported objects keep their script fallback. Restarting the map is optional; if automatic communication is unavailable, launch or reload the map from the game after installation. Keep the target game and edited map consistent with the open project.
